synopsis: SALT AND ASH. The tile breaks first. At the rim of the hole on the twenty-third day, with the seal spoken and Denet Rasca named the finder, Ysoly Tamm has the requirement word for word and two named witnesses standing either side of her - and before she speaks she counts them again, because that is what she has done at the tailgate of the ninth wagon every dusk for thirty years. The clay lets go between her hand and the Warden's. She says the sentence over the halves and it is worth nothing: a tile broken before the speaking of it is no licence, and he that holds no licence may require nothing. No requirement, no season, no clock. Iseul Fane will not say whether she hurried, because she does not know. At first light the joint tile brings two hundred people past the hole to look down into it - exactly what Sabra Onn demanded on the rock, and worth nothing either - and the hole is filled with the Tamm Line's own hundred dumped blocks and held under a lead disc on an iron pin. The packet goes off the ground in the finder's hand, because the seal has no reach over paper, and the Line goes to Tallow Reach inside Master Sarn's tile. At the far rim the weighbridge takes the tally-stick and will not enter the water; the Level House takes the four lines Denet should have entered in the spring, and a fifth for the volume off Ysoly's notches, six hours before Vask's letter comes up in the depot bag and the College lifts his seal. The record ends complete, correct and public, and moves nothing, because to check a line of it a man must stand on ground the Wardenry holds and the Wardenry appoints the surveyor. Iseul enters the seal with eleven days to spare, writes that the Wardenry owes itself, and takes a seat at Bell Harrow to be in the room where the surveyor is appointed; he is not appointed. Denet is paid four blocks and a quarter for the ground and works out that he came out of the water at the centre of the Meniscus a quarter of a block to the good. Vask keeps every term he ever wrote, and Enna Corrow will not go on any paper at fourteen. Ysoly sells the Line at the arriving price, comes home on somebody else's way-bill as one woman with her own water, and gets the roof she wanted and nothing left in the room to count twice. The water stays in the ground. In the spring the crossings walk past the seal on the twentieth day and the string drinks brine off a cut lid nine feet above it, and at dusk Hanei goes down the line, counts the butts, turns round and counts them again.
title: The Far Side
